office: the National Identification and Registration Authority (NIRA)

routes.label: in person at a NIRA office, for biometrics; collected at the place of residence

note: NIRA's 2025 registration and renewal drive: the Minister of State for Internal Affairs, launching it (The Observer, 6 May 2025), listed new registrations for both children and adults as free, renewals of expired cards free, a change of particulars Shs 200,000 and a lost card's replacement Shs 50,000 (replacements and changes not modelled); Pulse Uganda gives the same. An adult's first registration needs a local leader's letter or a citizenship certificate. Whether registration stays free after the drive isn't stated; it is modelled as free. The card's term and the time aren't stated. NIRA's own site serves its pages only through a script this session couldn't run.

sources.title: Pulse Uganda, When and how to renew your Ugandan national ID (June 2025)
sources.said: There are no fees for renewing your National ID. ... A fee of Shs 50,000 applies for replacing a lost ID, and Shs 200,000 applies for correcting or changing personal details. ... For children under 18, registration is free, provided a parent or blood relative’s National ID is presented. Adults registering for the first time will need additional documentation such as a local leader’s letter or a citizenship certificate from the Directorate of Citizenship and Immigration Control.

sources.title: The Observer (Uganda), Uganda national ID registration and renewal to begin May 27 - Muhoozi (6 May 2025)
sources.said: Services to be offered include free renewals of expired IDs, new registrations for both children and adults (free), change or correction of particulars Shs 200,000. Replacement of lost cards will cost Shs 50,000.
